title: Delhi to Roll Out 1,300 Pink Electric Autos Driven by Women and Transgender Drivers
excerpt: The DURGA scheme makes women and transgender beneficiaries owners as well as drivers, combining self-employment with safer, cleaner last-mile transport in the capital.
body:
• Delhi's Cabinet has approved the DURGA (Driving, Upliftment and Rozgar for Women and Transgender) E-Auto Scheme, allocating 1,300 pink electric autos in the first phase — 1,170 for women and 130 for transgender beneficiaries.
  • Beneficiaries will own and drive the vehicles: each revenue district gets up to 90 autos for women and 10 for transgender persons, allocated through a dedicated NIC digital portal with an online draw of lots if applications exceed quota.
  • Eligibility: Delhi resident, aged 20-40, with voter ID, LMV driving licence and public-service-vehicle badge; transgender applicants also need a District Magistrate certificate; family income for 2025-26 must not exceed ₹5 lakh.
  • The scheme combines self-employment with safer, cleaner last-mile connectivity — autos carry DURGA branding, a three-year lock-in, free aggregator onboarding, and charging/parking space at 70 metro stations.

What DURGA does

The Delhi Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, approved the scheme on September 23, 2026, under the full name 'Driving, Upliftment and Rozgar for Women and Transgender Green E-Auto'. It is a deliberate two-for-one policy: expand cleaner urban transport while opening a dignified, independent livelihood for groups that remain underrepresented in the transport sector.

Unlike driver-employment programs, DURGA makes the beneficiaries owners as well as drivers. Selected applicants receive Letters of Intent, identity cards, and DURGA-branded jackets and caps; the pink autos carry distinct identification so passengers can recognize them easily. The vehicles carry a mandatory three-year lock-in during which they cannot be sold or transferred.

"The objective of the DURGA Scheme goes beyond the allocation of electric vehicles. It is about creating opportunities for women and transgender persons to build independent livelihoods, participate more actively in the transport sector and become self-reliant."

— Pankaj Kumar Singh, Delhi Transport Minister

The numbers

The district math is neat: 1,170 women's autos divided by 90 per district and 130 transgender autos divided by 10 per district both point to 13 revenue districts covered. District Magistrate-led committees will check applications every week; if eligible applicants exceed the available quota, selection happens through an online draw of lots. Applications will run through a digital portal developed by the National Informatics Centre, Delhi — though the government has not yet announced when the portal will open.

Supporting infrastructure is already being arranged: the Transport Department has requested dedicated parking and charging spaces at Metro and Namo Bharat RRTS stations from DMRC and NCRTC, and charging space has been made available at 70 metro station parking areas. Aggregators will be asked to provide free onboarding and subscriptions to help drivers join digital mobility platforms, and beneficiaries can also claim applicable incentives under the Delhi EV Policy 2026.

Eligibility at a glance

The announced conditions for women applicants: Delhi resident, aged 20 to 40, valid voter ID, light motor vehicle driving licence and public service vehicle (PSV) badge, not more than three children, neither the applicant nor her family may own a registered transport vehicle or three-wheeler, and family income for FY 2025-26 not above ₹5 lakh. Transgender applicants must additionally present a transgender certificate issued by a Delhi district magistrate's office. The licence-and-documentation bar is real: analysts note the PSV badge and paperwork requirements may limit initial uptake, and a two-phase assessment will review the scheme's impact on beneficiaries' livelihoods.

Why it matters for Delhi's streets

The Transport Minister's pitch is that autos driven by women and transgender persons will build public confidence and make last-mile transport "more accessible and inclusive," particularly during early morning and late evening hours — the trips where women's safety concerns are sharpest. For the diaspora visiting or with family in Delhi, the practical effect is a new, recognizable option for short trips: look for the pink DURGA-branded autos, with drivers who are owners rather than hired hands. More on the rollout is available via WebIndia123, Adda247 and Nation Press.

What's next

The immediate watch item is the portal opening date and procurement timetable, which the government has not announced — those details decide how fast 1,300 autos move from cabinet approval to Delhi's roads. The two-phase assessment of livelihood impact will be the measure of whether DURGA becomes a template for other states or a one-off announcement.
